name: Untere Isar & Karwendelschlucht
kurzbeschreibung: The Untere Isar-Klamm is an impressive rock gorge with roaring waters and adventurous walkways along the Isar.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lower Isar and its rugged canyon gorges within the Karwendel Nature Park—spanning between Scharnitz, the Hinterautal, and Hinterriss—rank among the last truly untamed wild river landscapes in Central Europe. Originating from pristine underground limestone springs deep inside the Karwendel Range, the young Isar river carves through colossal limestone formations, fashioning a dynamic mosaic of deeply incised canyons, expansive white gravel bars, turquoise pools, and primeval riparian woodlands. Cradled within the largest contiguous nature reserve in the Eastern Alps, the valley harbors extraordinary alpine biodiversity: constantly shifting gravel shores provide vital sanctuaries for endangered pioneer flora like the German tamarisk, as well as specialized bird species including the common sandpiper and white-throated dipper. For nature enthusiasts, hikers, fly fishers, and packrafters, the river canyon provides an unmatched sanctuary of raw alpine purity.

Route & Requirements

Exploring the Isar canyon landscape delivers delightful excursions for all abilities. The signature trek follows the Isar Origin Trail departing from Scharnitz: extending roughly 6 to 8 kilometers, a well-maintained, gently graded gravel and woodland path traces the rushing turquoise riverbed through dramatic canyon narrows toward Gleirschhöhe (walking time 2 to 2.5 hours, easy grade T1/T2, suitable for rugged all-terrain strollers). Another breathtaking sector lies near Hinterriss in the Rißtal valley, where educational boardwalks and cantilevered viewing platforms suspend visitors directly over churning rapids and gravel islands. Active hikers can branch into the rugged Gleirschklamm gorge (grade T2, secured rock paths with wire cables). During warm months, the river is also prized by experienced white-water kayakers and packrafters. Sturdy hiking shoes, sun hats, and compact binoculars are recommended. Leashed dogs are welcome on all trails and enjoy cooling off along gentle gravel shores.

Visit & Arrival

Rail transit arrives via regional ÖBB or German Werdenfelsbahn trains into Scharnitz station on the Tyrolean-Bavarian border. From the platform, signposted walking paths reach the Karwendel Nature Park trailheads in ten minutes. Seasonal hiking buses link Hinterriss with Lenggries and Jenbach. Drivers reach Scharnitz via federal highway B177 from Innsbruck or Garmisch-Partenkirchen. Spacious pay parking is located at the Karwendeltäler Länd parking grounds in Scharnitz.

Tips

Take an extended break on the sun-warmed white gravel bars: the icy, crystal-clear water offers an invigorating natural Kneipp therapy for tired feet against the dramatic panorama of vertical Karwendel rock faces. Stop at the interactive Karwendel Nature Park Information Center in Scharnitz or the Nature Park House in Hinterriss to discover the fascinating hydrology of wild rivers.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Winterwanderung bei geräumtem Weg möglich)
